in_hebrew.name: יָרֵב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'yarab' meaning to surround, encompass, or protect. The name Jareb can be interpreted as 'one who is surrounded by thorns', 'thicket of thorns', or 'thorny one'. This name appears in the Hebrew Bible as the name of an Ishmaelite who was one of the leaders of the raiding parties against the Israelites (Genesis 26:14-15, 33:1-2).

in_greek.name: Ἰαρέβ
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Ἰαρέβ is derived from the Hebrew name יָרֵב (Yareb). It retains the same meaning as the Hebrew name and can be translated as 'thicket of thorns' or 'thorny one'. Jareb appears in the Greek Septuagint as the name of the Ishmaelite leader mentioned in Genesis 26:14-15, 33:1-2.

in_latin.name: Iarob
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Iarob is a Latinization of the Greek name Ἰαρέβ (Iareb). It preserves the same meaning as the Greek and Hebrew names and can be translated as 'thicket of thorns' or 'thorny one'.
